summary: First testing pass over the Clipper UI/UX refinement. Ran a new pytest suite against the preview backend (6/6 pass) covering the new /api/caption-options categories, the ClipRecipe caption_color/caption_active_color/captions_on pass-through, the ASS recolour on export, and the captions-off suppression of the .ass file. Ran Playwright flows across the landing page, theme toggle + persistence, source tabs + continue button 'empty slot', the demo-job-0001 results page with the singular '1 clip ready' toast, the clip editor (Burn captions in switch, colour swatch rows, Vibrant + Clean categories, 'c' keyboard shortcut), an end-to-end colour override + export, and a fresh UI registration + dashboard in both light and dark themes.

ui_bugs.issue: In dark theme .marquee { background: var(--ink); color: #fff } becomes white-on-white because --ink is #f2f1ee in dark mode. The whole scrolling feature strip is unreadable in dark theme.

After clicking [data-testid=export-clip-btn] the render clearly finishes on the backend (clip_1.mp4 and clip_1.ass are rewritten with the new colour) but the 'Clip exported' <strong> confirmation was NOT found in the DOM 30s later — the view had returned to the results/clips overlay. Either the confirmation is auto-dismissed very quickly or navigation happens on completion, hiding it. Please verify the exported=true toast/inline confirmation is actually surfaced to the user.

Space did not toggle play/pause and ArrowRight did not scrub the playhead in the automated run (video currentTime stayed at 0). This may be because the preview <video> source was still loading during the test (a 'The element has no supported sources' pageerror was observed once), but please verify Space/Arrow shortcuts fire before the video is fully loaded, and that focus handling is correct. 'c' toggle for captions works.

issues: Marquee row renders white text on a near-white bar (ratio ~1.1) — hard-coded --ink usage breaks in inverted palette. See .marquee rule.

action_items: Fix .marquee background/text so it uses a stable dark ink (e.g. a fixed #14141a or a new --marquee-bg token) rather than var(--ink), which flips in dark mode.
Verify the 'Clip exported' confirmation is user-visible after an editor export (was not detected in DOM 30s post-click during the automated run, though the backend export succeeded).

Verify the editor's Space / ArrowLeft / ArrowRight shortcuts actually reach the video element and change currentTime; the automated run saw no change (may be a video-loading race in the test rather than a real bug).
critical_code_review_comments: polish.css dark-theme layer inverts --ink to a light value but styles.css still references var(--ink) as a dark surface (e.g. .marquee). Any base-layer rule that treated --ink as 'dark' needs auditing; consider a semantic token like --surface-inverse.

backend/app/main.py still hardcodes CORSMiddleware allow_origins to localhost only. Preview/prod origins work here because the ingress rewrites /api to this app, but a stricter deployment would break the browser client.
ClipRecipe declares `speed: Optional[float] = None` twice (lines ~651 and ~665) — the second declaration silently overwrites the first. Cosmetic, but worth cleaning.
test_credentials: Registered ad-hoc via UI (TEST_* / testuser_* @test.com, password testpass123). No seeded accounts.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing demo-job-0001. Backend tests overwrite clip_1.ass on demo-job-0001; if that becomes an issue rerun /app/backend/seed_demo.py.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend caption-refinement API is solid (6/6 pytest). Editor UI works end-to-end: Burn captions toggle correctly hides the style picker/swatch rows and suppresses the .ass file on export; colour swatches change PrimaryColour in the ASS file (verified: #ff9000 -> &H000090FF). The main outstanding items are (1) the marquee dark-mode contrast bug on the landing page, (2) confirming the 'Clip exported' visual confirmation actually appears to a real user, and (3) verifying the keyboard shortcut wiring for Space/Arrows on the editor video. Dashboard renders correctly in both themes. Note: to run backend tests do `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview> /root/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_editor_backend.py -v`.
rca of the issue: Marquee dark-theme bug: styles.css defines .marquee with background: var(--ink). polish.css inverts --ink for html[data-theme='dark'] to #f2f1ee (a near-white). Since --ink was used both as the site's primary text colour AND as a dark surface (the marquee bar), the inversion flips the marquee to white while its text remains hardcoded to #fff. Mitigation: introduce a separate token (e.g. --ink-solid or --marquee-bg) that stays dark in both themes, or hardcode the marquee bar to a fixed near-black.
